They:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eStart with minimal context (just what they need)\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eExecute granular, linear tasks with clear boundaries\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eDocument their work in shared memory\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eTerminate upon completion\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eShared Knowledge Graph (RAG)\u003c/strong\u003e\u003cbr\u003e\nInstead of cramming everything into context windows:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003ePersistent memory stores all project knowledge\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eAgents query only what's relevant to their task\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eKnowledge accumulates without overwhelming any single agent\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eClear separation between working memory and reference material\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eResult\u003c/strong\u003e: Agents that are fast, focused, and safe. They can't be manipulated to reveal full project details because they never have access to it all at once.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch3 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eWhy This Matters for Safety\u003c/h3\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-why-this-matters-for-safety\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: Why This Matters for Safety\" href=\"#why-this-matters-for-safety\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eTraditional long-context agents are like giving someone your entire codebase, documentation, and secrets in one conversation. Your development speed is limited only by how well you decompose tasks.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eNo More Lost Context\u003c/strong\u003e\u003cbr\u003e\nEvery decision, implementation detail, and architectural choice is stored in the shared knowledge graph. New agents instantly understand the project state without reading through lengthy conversation histories.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003ePredictable, Reliable Outputs\u003c/strong\u003e\u003cbr\u003e\nFocused agents with limited context produce consistent results. The same task produces the same quality output every time, making development predictable and testable.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eBuilt-in Conflict Prevention\u003c/strong\u003e\u003cbr\u003e\nFile-level locking and task assignment prevent agents from stepping on each other's work. No more merge conflicts from simultaneous edits.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eComplete Development Transparency\u003c/strong\u003e\u003cbr\u003e\nWatch your AI team work in real-time through the dashboard. Every action is logged, every decision traceable. It's like having a live view into your development pipeline.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eFor Different Team Sizes\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eSolo Developers\u003c/strong\u003e: Transform one AI assistant into a coordinated team. Work on multiple features simultaneously without losing track.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eSmall Teams\u003c/strong\u003e: Augment human developers with AI specialists that maintain perfect context across sessions.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eLarge Projects\u003c/strong\u003e: Handle complex systems where no single agent could hold all the context. <p dir="auto"><a href="https://deepwiki.com/rinadelph/Agent-MCP" rel="nofollow"><img src="https://camo.githubusercontent.com/0f5ae213ac378635adeb5d7f13cef055ad2f7d9a47b36de7b1c67dbe09f609ca/68747470733a2f2f6465657077696b692e636f6d2f62616467652e737667" alt="Ask DeepWiki" data-canonical-src="https://deepwiki.com/badge.svg" style="max-width: 100%;"></a></p>
<blockquote>
<p dir="auto">🚀 <strong>Advanced Tool Notice</strong>: This framework is designed for experienced AI developers who need sophisticated multi-agent orchestration capabilities. Agent-MCP requires familiarity with AI coding workflows, MCP protocols, and distributed systems concepts. We're actively working to improve documentation and ease of use. If you're new to AI-assisted development, consider starting with simpler tools and returning when you need advanced multi-agent capabilities.</p>
<p dir="auto">💬 <strong>Join the Community</strong>: Connect with us on <a href="https://discord.gg/7Jm7nrhjGn" rel="nofollow">Discord</a> to get help, share experiences, and collaborate with other developers building multi-agent systems.</p>
</blockquote>
<p dir="auto">Multi-Agent Collaboration Protocol for coordinated AI software development.</p>
<div align="center" dir="auto">
  <a target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" href="/rinadelph/Agent-MCP/blob/main/assets/images/agent-network-viz.png"><img src="/rinadelph/Agent-MCP/raw/main/assets/images/agent-network-viz.png" alt="Agent Network Visualization" width="600" style="max-width: 100%;"></a>
</div>
<p dir="auto">Think <strong>Obsidian for your AI agents</strong> - a living knowledge graph where multiple AI agents collaborate through shared context, intelligent task management, and real-time visualization. Watch your codebase evolve as specialized agents work in parallel, never losing context or stepping on each other's work.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Why Multiple Agents?</h2><a id="user-content-why-multiple-agents" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Why Multiple Agents?" href="#why-multiple-agents"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Beyond the philosophical issues, traditional AI coding assistants hit practical limitations:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><strong>Context windows overflow</strong> on large codebases</li>
<li><strong>Knowledge gets lost</strong> between conversations</li>
<li><strong>Single-threaded execution</strong> creates bottlenecks</li>
<li><strong>No specialization</strong> - one agent tries to do everything</li>
<li><strong>Constant rework</strong> from lost context and confusion</li>
</ul>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">The Multi-Agent Solution</h2><a id="user-content-the-multi-agent-solution" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: The Multi-Agent Solution" href="#the-multi-agent-solution"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Agent-MCP transforms AI development from a single assistant to a coordinated team:</p>
<div align="center" dir="auto">
  <a target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" href="/rinadelph/Agent-MCP/blob/main/assets/images/dashboard-overview.png"><img src="/rinadelph/Agent-MCP/raw/main/assets/images/dashboard-overview.png" alt="Multi-Agent Collaboration Network" width="800" style="max-width: 100%;"></a>
</div>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Real-time visualization</strong> shows your AI team at work - purple nodes represent context entries, blue nodes are agents, and connections show active collaborations. It's like having a mission control center for your development team.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Core Capabilities</h3><a id="user-content-core-capabilities" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Core Capabilities" href="#core-capabilities"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Parallel Execution</strong><br>
Multiple specialized agents work simultaneously on different parts of your codebase. Backend agents handle APIs while frontend agents build UI components, all coordinated through shared memory.</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Persistent Knowledge Graph</strong></p>
<div align="center" dir="auto">
  <a target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" href="/rinadelph/Agent-MCP/blob/main/assets/images/memory-bank.png"><img src="/rinadelph/Agent-MCP/raw/main/assets/images/memory-bank.png" alt="Memory Bank Interface" width="800" style="max-width: 100%;"></a>
</div>
<p dir="auto">Your project's entire context lives in a searchable, persistent memory bank. Agents query this shared knowledge to understand requirements, architectural decisions, and implementation details. Nothing gets lost between sessions.</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Intelligent Task Management</strong></p>
<div align="center" dir="auto">
  <a target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" href="/rinadelph/Agent-MCP/blob/main/assets/images/agent-fleet.png"><img src="/rinadelph/Agent-MCP/raw/main/assets/images/agent-fleet.png" alt="Agent Fleet Management" width="800" style="max-width: 100%;"></a>
</div>
<p dir="auto">Monitor every agent's status, assigned tasks, and recent activity. The system automatically manages task dependencies, prevents conflicts, and ensures work flows smoothly from planning to implementation.</p>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">What is MCP?</h3><a id="user-content-what-is-mcp" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: What is MCP?" href="#what-is-mcp"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">The <strong>Model Context Protocol (MCP)</strong> is an open standard that enables AI assistants to securely connect to external data sources and tools. Agent-MCP leverages MCP to provide seamless integration with various development tools and services.</p>

<p dir="auto">Create an MCP configuration file (<code>mcp_config.json</code>):</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-json notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto"><pre>{
  <span class="pl-ent">"server"</span>: {
    <span class="pl-ent">"name"</span>: <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>agent-mcp<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>,
    <span class="pl-ent">"version"</span>: <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>1.0.0<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>
  },
  <span class="pl-ent">"tools"</span>: [
    {
      <span class="pl-ent">"name"</span>: <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>create_agent<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>,
      <span class="pl-ent">"description"</span>: <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>Create a new specialized AI agent<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>
    },
    {
      <span class="pl-ent">"name"</span>: <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>assign_task<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>, 
      <span class="pl-ent">"description"</span>: <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>Assign tasks to specific agents<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>
    },
    {
      <span class="pl-ent">"name"</span>: <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>query_project_context<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>,
      <span class="pl-ent">"description"</span>: <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>Query the shared knowledge graph<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>
    },
    {
      <span class="pl-ent">"name"</span>: <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>manage_agent_communication<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>,
      <span class="pl-ent">"description"</span>: <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>Handle inter-agent messaging<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>
    }
  ],
  <span class="pl-ent">"resources"</span>: [
    {
      <span class="pl-ent">"name"</span>: <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>agent_status<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>,
      <span class="pl-ent">"description"</span>: <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>Real-time agent status and activity<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>
    },
    {
      <span class="pl-ent">"name"</span>: <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>project_memory<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>,

<p dir="auto">Once connected, you can use these MCP tools directly in Claude:</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Agent Management</strong></p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><code>create_agent</code> - Spawn specialized agents (backend, frontend, testing, etc.)</li>
<li><code>list_agents</code> - View all active agents and their status</li>
<li><code>terminate_agent</code> - Safely shut down agents</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Task Orchestration</strong></p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><code>assign_task</code> - Delegate work to specific agents</li>
<li><code>view_tasks</code> - Monitor task progress and dependencies</li>
<li><code>update_task_status</code> - Track completion and blockers</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Knowledge Management</strong></p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><code>ask_project_rag</code> - Query the persistent knowledge graph</li>
<li><code>update_project_context</code> - Add architectural decisions and patterns</li>
<li><code>view_project_context</code> - Access stored project information</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Communication</strong></p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><code>send_agent_message</code> - Direct messaging between agents</li>
<li><code>broadcast_message</code> - Send updates to all agents</li>
<li><code>request_assistance</code> - Escalate complex issues</li>
</ul>

from mcp import Client

async def main():
    async with Client("http://localhost:8000/mcp") as client:
        # Create a backend agent
        result = await client.call_tool("create_agent", {
            "role": "backend",
            "specialization": "API development"
        })
        
        # Assign a task
        await client.call_tool("assign_task", {

        })
        
        # Query project context

        })

<ul dir="auto">

<li>UI component hierarchies and workflows</li>

</ul>

<li>Type <code>#</code> to open Claude's memory feature</li>
<li>Paste the instructions for persistent behavior</li>

<p dir="auto">The system maintains several types of memory:</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Project Context</strong> - Architectural decisions, design patterns, conventions<br>
<strong>Task Memory</strong> - Current status, blockers, implementation notes<br>
<strong>Agent Memory</strong> - Individual agent learnings and specializations<br>
<strong>Integration Points</strong> - How different components connect</p>
<p dir="auto">All memory is:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>Searchable via semantic queries</li>
<li>Version controlled for rollback</li>
<li>Tagged for easy categorization</li>
<li>Automatically garbage collected when stale</li>
</ul>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Conflict Resolution</h3><a id="user-content-conflict-resolution" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Conflict Resolution" href="#conflict-resolution"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">File-level locking prevents agents from overwriting each other's work:</p>
<ol dir="auto">
<li>Agent requests file access</li>
<li>System checks if file is locked</li>
<li>If locked, agent works on other tasks or waits</li>
<li>After completion, lock is released</li>
<li>Other agents can now modify the file</li>
</ol>
<p dir="auto">This happens automatically - no manual coordination needed.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Short-Lived vs. Long-Lived Agents: The Critical Difference</h2><a id="user-content-short-lived-vs-long-lived-agents-the-critical-difference" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Short-Lived vs. Long-Lived Agents: The Critical Difference" href="#short-lived-vs-long-lived-agents-the-critical-difference"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Traditional Long-Lived Agents</h3><a id="user-content-traditional-long-lived-agents" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Traditional Long-Lived Agents" href="#traditional-long-lived-agents"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Most AI coding assistants maintain conversations across entire projects:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><strong>Accumulated context grows unbounded</strong> - mixing unrelated code, decisions, and conversations</li>
<li><strong>Confused priorities</strong> - yesterday's bug fix mingles with today's feature request</li>
<li><strong>Hallucination risks increase</strong> - agents invent connections between unrelated parts</li>
<li><strong>Performance degrades over time</strong> - every response processes irrelevant history</li>
<li><strong>Security vulnerability</strong> - one carefully crafted prompt could expose your entire project</li>
</ul>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Agent-MCP's Ephemeral Agents</h3><a id="user-content-agent-mcps-ephemeral-agents" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Agent-MCP's Ephemeral Agents" href="#agent-mcps-ephemeral-agents"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Each agent is purpose-built for a single task:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><strong>Minimal, focused context</strong> - only what's needed for the specific task</li>
<li><strong>Crystal clear objectives</strong> - one task, one goal, no ambiguity</li>
<li><strong>Deterministic behavior</strong> - limited context means predictable outputs</li>
<li><strong>Consistently fast responses</strong> - no context bloat to slow things down</li>
<li><strong>Secure by design</strong> - agents literally cannot access what they don't need</li>
</ul>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">The Theory Behind Linear Decomposition</h2><a id="user-content-the-theory-behind-linear-decomposition" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: The Theory Behind Linear Decomposition" href="#the-theory-behind-linear-decomposition"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">The Philosophy: Short-Lived Agents, Granular Tasks</h3><a id="user-content-the-philosophy-short-lived-agents-granular-tasks" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: The Philosophy: Short-Lived Agents, Granular Tasks" href="#the-philosophy-short-lived-agents-granular-tasks"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Most AI development approaches suffer from a fundamental flaw: they try to maintain massive context windows with a single, long-running agent. This leads to:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><strong>Context pollution</strong> - Irrelevant information drowns out what matters</li>
<li><strong>Hallucination risks</strong> - Agents invent connections between unrelated parts</li>
<li><strong>Security vulnerabilities</strong> - Agents with full context can be manipulated</li>
<li><strong>Performance degradation</strong> - Large contexts slow down reasoning</li>
<li><strong>Unpredictable behavior</strong> - Too much context creates chaos</li>
</ul>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Our Solution: Ephemeral Agents with Shared Memory</h3><a id="user-content-our-solution-ephemeral-agents-with-shared-memory" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Our Solution: Ephemeral Agents with Shared Memory" href="#our-solution-ephemeral-agents-with-shared-memory"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Agent-MCP implements a radically different approach:</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Short-Lived, Focused Agents</strong><br>
Each agent lives only as long as their specific task. They:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>Start with minimal context (just what they need)</li>
<li>Execute granular, linear tasks with clear boundaries</li>
<li>Document their work in shared memory</li>
<li>Terminate upon completion</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Shared Knowledge Graph (RAG)</strong><br>
Instead of cramming everything into context windows:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>Persistent memory stores all project knowledge</li>
<li>Agents query only what's relevant to their task</li>
<li>Knowledge accumulates without overwhelming any single agent</li>
<li>Clear separation between working memory and reference material</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Result</strong>: Agents that are fast, focused, and safe. They can't be manipulated to reveal full project details because they never have access to it all at once.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Why This Matters for Safety</h3><a id="user-content-why-this-matters-for-safety" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Why This Matters for Safety" href="#why-this-matters-for-safety"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Traditional long-context agents are like giving someone your entire codebase, documentation, and secrets in one conversation. Our approach is like having specialized contractors who only see the blueprint for their specific room.</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><strong>Reduced attack surface</strong> - Agents can't leak what they don't know</li>
<li><strong>Deterministic behavior</strong> - Limited context means predictable outputs</li>
<li><strong>Audit trails</strong> - Every agent action is logged and traceable</li>
<li><strong>Rollback capability</strong> - Mistakes are isolated to specific tasks</li>
</ul>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">The Cleanup Protocol: Keeping Your System Lean</h3><a id="user-content-the-cleanup-protocol-keeping-your-system-lean" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: The Cleanup Protocol: Keeping Your System Lean" href="#the-cleanup-protocol-keeping-your-system-lean"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Agent-MCP enforces strict lifecycle management:</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Maximum 10 Active Agents</strong></p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>Hard limit prevents resource exhaustion</li>
<li>Forces thoughtful task allocation</li>
<li>Maintains system performance</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Automatic Cleanup Rules</strong></p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>Agent finishes task → Immediately terminated</li>
<li>Agent idle 60+ seconds → Killed and task reassigned</li>
<li>Need more than 10 agents → Least productive agents removed</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Why This Matters</strong></p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><strong>No zombie processes</strong> eating resources</li>
<li><strong>Fresh context</strong> for every task</li>
<li><strong>Predictable resource usage</strong></li>
<li><strong>Clean system state</strong> always</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">This isn't just housekeeping - it's fundamental to the security and performance benefits of the short-lived agent model.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">The Fundamental Principle</h3><a id="user-content-the-fundamental-principle" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: The Fundamental Principle" href="#the-fundamental-principle"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Any task that cannot be expressed as <code>Step 1 → Step 2 → Step N</code> is not atomic enough.</strong></p>
<p dir="auto">This principle drives everything in Agent-MCP:</p>
<ol dir="auto">
<li><strong>Complex goals</strong> must decompose into <strong>linear sequences</strong></li>
<li><strong>Linear sequences</strong> can execute <strong>in parallel</strong> when independent</li>
<li><strong>Each step</strong> must have <strong>clear prerequisites</strong> and <strong>deterministic outputs</strong></li>
<li><strong>Integration points</strong> are <strong>explicit</strong> and <strong>well-defined</strong></li>
</ol>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Why Linear Decomposition Works</h3><a id="user-content-why-linear-decomposition-works" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Why Linear Decomposition Works" href="#why-linear-decomposition-works"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>

<p dir="auto">Each step is atomic, testable, and has zero ambiguity. Multiple agents can work these chains in parallel without conflict.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Why Developers Choose Agent-MCP</h2><a id="user-content-why-developers-choose-agent-mcp" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Why Developers Choose Agent-MCP" href="#why-developers-choose-agent-mcp"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto"><strong>The Power of Parallel Development</strong><br>
Instead of waiting for one agent to finish the backend before starting the frontend, deploy specialized agents to work simultaneously. Your development speed is limited only by how well you decompose tasks.</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>No More Lost Context</strong><br>
Every decision, implementation detail, and architectural choice is stored in the shared knowledge graph. New agents instantly understand the project state without reading through lengthy conversation histories.</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Predictable, Reliable Outputs</strong><br>
Focused agents with limited context produce consistent results. The same task produces the same quality output every time, making development predictable and testable.</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Built-in Conflict Prevention</strong><br>
File-level locking and task assignment prevent agents from stepping on each other's work. No more merge conflicts from simultaneous edits.</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Complete Development Transparency</strong><br>
Watch your AI team work in real-time through the dashboard. Every action is logged, every decision traceable. It's like having a live view into your development pipeline.</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>For Different Team Sizes</strong></p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Solo Developers</strong>: Transform one AI assistant into a coordinated team. Work on multiple features simultaneously without losing track.</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Small Teams</strong>: Augment human developers with AI specialists that maintain perfect context across sessions.</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Large Projects</strong>: Handle complex systems where no single agent could hold all the context. The shared memory scales infinitely.</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Learning & Teaching</strong>: Perfect for understanding software architecture. Watch how tasks decompose and integrate in real-time.</p>

<p dir="auto"><strong>"Admin token not found"</strong><br>
Check the server startup logs - token is displayed when MCP server starts.</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>"Worker can't access tasks"</strong><br>
Ensure you're using the worker token (not admin token) when initializing workers.</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>"Agents overwriting each other"</strong><br>
Verify all workers are initialized with the <code>--worker</code> flag for proper coordination.</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>"Dashboard connection failed"</strong></p>
<ol dir="auto">
<li>Ensure MCP server is running first</li>
<li>Check Node.js version (18+ required)</li>
<li>Reinstall dashboard dependencies</li>
</ol>
<p dir="auto"><strong>"Memory queries returning stale data"</strong><br>
Run memory garbage collection through the dashboard or restart with <code>--refresh-memory</code>.</p>
